text.p: This is how major world bond markets were trading in late European business on Tuesday.

GERMANY - German Bunds and futures were higher but off the session peaks in late dealings on Tuesday as cash market 10-year yields remained below the psychologically important six percent level, traders said. The December Bund future on the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange (LIFFE) was trading at 99.55, up 0.24 from Monday's settlement price.

BRITAIN - Gilts settled higher on Tuesday, buoyed by the unrelenting climb in sterling and signs of moderating high street sales strength. The December long gilt future on LIFFE was trading at 110-23/32, up 09/32 from Monday's settlement price.

FRANCE - French bond and PIBOR futures ended a quiet session much higher on Tuesday, lifted by a return of domestic buyers to the market after Monday's consolidation. The December notional bond future on the MATIF in Paris settled at 126.44, up 0.50 from Monday's settlement price.

ITALY - Italian bonds and futures maintained their buoyant tone, fuelled by dollar strength and a subsequent firming of the lira, but the 10-year Btp closed off its day's high and volume was thin, dealers said. The December bond future on LIFFE was trading at 123.17, up 0.19 from Monday's settlement price.

UNITED STATES - U.S. Treasuries were modestly higher in moderate midday trade as investors remained in a waiting mood ahead of the release of the key September consumer price index on Wednesday, analysts said. The December Treasury bond future on the Chicago Board of Trade was trading at 110-20/32, up 01/32 from Friday's settlement price. The long bond was quoted to yield 6.84 percent.

JAPAN - The key December Japanese government bond futures contract closed firmer after having overcome dealers' interest in selling-on-recoveries. In after hours trading the December future on LIFFE was trading at 122.94, down 0.02 from Monday's settlement price on the Tokyo Stock Exchange.

EUROBONDS - The primary market was hit by a rapid succession of new issues in dollars, marks, lire, sterling and French francs which spanned the credit spectrum. A trio of $200 million bonds led the way in the early session at four-, six- and 10-year maturities. In the emerging market, Argentina launched a 500 billion lire seven-year bond which pays an 11.0 percent coupon. The Bank of Scotland and FEC tapped the sterling sector. Around 2.5 billion marks were raised while IMI Bank set a 2.0 billion French franc six-year bond.
